subject: ArgentEdge procurement: PO requirements, invoice cadence & net term options
messages:
From: Claire Bennett <claire.bennett@argentedge.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@argentedge.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO template + invoice cadence / net terms question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the cost controls. Procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of specifics so we can finalize the PO and payment flow:

- Their standard is a single blanket PO referencing a monthly invoice. They need each invoice to show the PO number, cost center, and a line-level breakdown. Can Redwood accommodate that format?
- ArgentEdge runs on Net90 for SaaS spend by default; is Net90 acceptable (or can we do Net60)? If Net90 is required we may need invoices to flow into our lockbox.
- On discounts: they asked whether we can get any additional list discount for a 12-month committed purchase vs month-to-month.
- Packaging question: do you sell committed capacity (reserved GPUs / dedicated throughput) vs consumption usage? If committed, what is the uplift in discount?

I attached our PO template for reference (ArgentEdge_PO_Template.pdf). If you can outline preferred commercial permutations (monthly invoice/netterm combos + how discounts change with commitment) that’ll help speed procurement.

Best,
Claire
Claire Bennett
Head of Procurement, ArgentEdge

Subject: Re: PO template + invoice cadence / net terms question

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (Finance) and Priyom (Sales Ops) to help with the payment mechanics. Short answers up front:

- PO line-level / cost-center: yes, we can include PO number and cost center on each invoice. We frequently populate the line-item description with model & route details (e.g., "dedicated-small: 4x3k token pools") when customers request it.
- Net terms: our default is Net45. For enterprise accounts we can consider Net60; Net90 is possible but typically requires a formal lockbox or ACH enrollment plus an underwriting review.
- Discounts & packaging: two clear options we commonly offer — committed 12-month subscription (fixed monthly invoice, deeper discount, preferred capacity routing) OR month-to-month usage (no long-term discount). See attached pricing grid for examples.

Proposed commercial buckets (high level):
1) 12-month committed plan — 10% list discount, monthly invoice, Net45, PO ok.
2) Quarterly prepay — 6% discount, quarterly invoice, Net45.
3) Consumption (month-to-month) — no commitment discount, Net45 by default.

If ArgentEdge must have Net90 we can do Net90 only if: (a) ACH/lockbox is enabled, (b) purchase order placed in advance for the committed term OR revenue holdback clause in SOW. Finance — is that close to what you’d accept? (Vanessa/Priyom: see "pricing_grid_v2.xlsx" attached — pricing examples are illustrative.)

Next step: Claire, if you can approximate ARR or a monthly spend band we’ll produce a clean option A/B quote to send to procurement.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Subject: RE: PO template + invoice cadence / net terms question

Quick internal note — copying into the thread so procurement sees our constraints.

We can be flexible for strategic accounts but need the following operational guardrails if we move off Net45:
- Net90 acceptance requires either: (1) lockbox/ACH with bank confirmation OR (2) a signed PO that covers at least 2 months of estimated invoice run-rate as a minimal credit buffer.
- Revenue recognition: longer payment windows increase credit exposure; if we allow Net90 without prepay we should add a 1.5% financing fee to compensate.
- Invoice cadence: monthly invoicing is preferred for reconciling usage/credits. If they insist on quarterly invoice we need a clear reconciliation clause for overage/true-up.
- Legal: any revenue-holdback clause or SLA-credit carve-out must be approved by Legal. I’ll flag BUF-legal for quick review.

I attached a short memo summarizing the finance risk (finance_risk_memo.docx).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Finance Operations

Subject: Re: PO template + invoice cadence / net terms question

Thanks — that helps. A few clarifications from our side after talking to AP:

- ArgentEdge prefers monthly invoices and would be comfortable with Net45 (good).
- For a 12-month commitment we can accept Net45 and are prepared to commit to the purchase if Redwood can confirm a 10% committed-discount (list) and dedicated capacity routing as described. That would make sign-off much faster.
- Net90 is a non-starter for our treasury unless it comes with an early-pay option: we can do Net90 only if merchants agree to a 2% early-pay discount for payment inside 30 days.

Attached is our filled PO template for your review (ArgentEdge_PO_Template_filled.pdf). Please confirm whether the 10% committed-discount + monthly invoices + Net45 path is acceptable and if legal/finance need anything else.

Claire

Claire — very helpful, and thank you for the prompt turnaround on the PO. We’re aligned enough to move to paperwork. Summary of the agreed commercial path and next steps: 

Commercially offered (pick one):
A) Committed 12-month subscription
   - 10% list discount (as requested)
   - Monthly invoices, each invoice includes PO number + cost center + line-level breakdown
   - Net45 payment terms (standard)
   - Dedicated routing profile for committed capacity

B) If ArgentEdge requires Net90
   - We can permit Net90 only with (i) ACH/lockbox enrollment AND (ii) a 2% financing fee OR a 2% early-pay discount option to encourage earlier remittance (your proposal). Invoices remain monthly and must reference the PO.

Operational & legal items:
- Vanessa & finance to open a lockbox/ACH onboarding ticket if they go with Net90.
- Priyom/Sales Ops will produce the final SOW and invoice template that matches the PO fields.
- Legal review: any holdback language or bespoke SLA credit handling will need Legal sign-off; I’ll route the SOW to Legal after you confirm the option.

Next steps for ArgentEdge:
1) Confirm whether you want Option A (preferred) or Option B.
2) If Option A: sign SOW + return PO, we’ll provision committed capacity and send first invoice the following month.
3) If Option B: return PO + start ACH enrollment (Vanessa, I’ll loop you separately with Claire for bank details).

I’ll prepare the formal quote and DocuSign SOW once you confirm. HubSpot deal and initial DocuSign envelope are linked here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-8923 and https://www.docusign.com/en/link/DocuSign-Envelope-8923

Thanks — excited to get ArgentEdge onboarded.
